assessment.summary: A rare, high-consequence impact; no known large object currently threatens Earth, though the catalogue of hazardous-size objects is incomplete — fewer than half of the estimated 140-meter-and-larger population has been found.
assessment.timeframe: No known object of concern is on an impact trajectory this century.

claims.text: NASA reports that no known asteroid larger than 140 meters has a significant chance of hitting Earth for the next 100 years.
NASA reports that fewer than half of the estimated 25,000 near-Earth objects 140 meters and larger have been found to date.
With over 90% of the near-Earth objects larger than one kilometer already discovered, NASA's NEO Observations Program is now focusing on finding 90% of the NEO population larger than 140 meters.

NASA raised the 2032 Earth-impact probability of asteroid 2024 YR4 to 3.1% on 18 February 2025, stating that this was 'the highest impact probability NASA has ever recorded for an object of this size or larger'; new data collected overnight reduced the impact probability to 1.5% the following day.

NASA states that asteroid 2024 YR4 poses no significant impact risk to Earth in 2032 and beyond, and that observations by the James Webb Space Telescope on 18 and 26 February ruled out any chance of the asteroid impacting the Moon on 22 December 2032, when it will instead fly by the Moon at a distance of 13,200 miles.

NASA's near-Earth asteroid tally as of 3 December 2025 records 39,123 discovered near-Earth asteroids of all sizes, of which 873 are larger than 1 kilometer with an estimated 50 left to be found, and 11,343 are larger than 140 meters with an estimated 14,000 remaining to be found.

description: A sufficiently large near-Earth object striking Earth would cause regional to continental devastation. NASA's Planetary Defense effort catalogues and tracks the larger near-Earth object population to assess impact hazards decades in advance, and reports that no known asteroid larger than 140 meters has a significant chance of hitting Earth for the next 100 years. The catalogue is still incomplete: as of December 2025 NASA counted 39,123 discovered near-Earth asteroids, including 873 larger than 1 kilometer with about 50 left to find, but only 11,343 larger than 140 meters with an estimated 14,000 still undiscovered. The system was tested in 2024-2026 by asteroid 2024 YR4, whose Earth-impact probability peaked at 3.1% in February 2025 — the highest NASA has ever recorded for an object of that size or larger — before follow-up observations, including from the James Webb Space Telescope, ruled out any impact of Earth or the Moon.
name: Near-Earth Asteroid Impact
